$schema_note: Conformance corpus for inspect_ai._view.scope (design/viewer-scoped-authorization.md section 7). cases: resolve `location` (null = absent, default binding) for `permission` under `scope`; `decode` names the route-layer decode applied first (path and query = one urllib.parse.unquote, the built-in resolving policies' rule; null = none); `platform` restricts a case (posix, windows, null = any). {tmp} is the resolved fixture root, {tmp_uri} its file: URI. claims: scope_from_claims validity. children: resolve_child. Claim root URIs must be absolute file/s3/gs/az/http(s) URIs; bare paths are accepted only by ScopeRoot.parse for the server's own log_dir.

cases.notes: a directory root refuses itself for read
a not-yet-existing subdirectory resolves through the nearest existing ancestor
after decode-once, ? is a file-name character in a bare path
route decoding is a single unquote; the literal path escapes and is refused (host and server can no longer disagree)
the same string with no route decoding is a literal path that escapes
after the single decode, ? in a file: URI is a file-name character too
a root given as a symlink is canonicalized to its target when the token is parsed
list on a file root means list exactly this file
remote paths reject .. components outright rather than normalizing them
no second decode: %2e%2e is a literal key component inside the root

claims.notes: unknown fields inside the claim are ignored
a claim root must be an absolute URI; bare paths never bind to the server cwd

children.notes: dir=%252Fhome%252Fvictim%252Fother after the server's single query decode; no second decode
